conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Nope, Mara. You're being painfully safe. Tell me why the disputed tattoo pact happened or at least invent a better lie.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Jules, that's bullshit. You don't get to dismiss me and then act surprised when I get angry about the forged apology letter.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: The current behavior is in stark contrast to the night someone stole the church bell. Jules is not a candidate for being the loser here. Jules is the one who can make an argument with no context and a clear point in the context of Jules's situation.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: You have made me understand the tension that the previous conversation would elicit and the absurdity of the potential secret within our shared memory of the night someone stole the church bell.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: I'm sorry, Owen. I didn't mean to hurt your feelings. It was an accident, and I'm not mad at you anymore. I just feel a bit disappointed. Can I come to a more positive place with you today?

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: I've understood what the conversation has elicited and why we have a secret we didn't reveal, but how will we get to the heart of it without betraying who we have betrayed so far.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: I want to make sure this is a breakthrough, but how can we ensure the suspicious key in Mara's coat really happened? Can we find it or not? Do we need any accomplice?

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Let's take it from here, and we're trying to ensure the key really did move. Do you know if it was with us, or were we not aware of its presence at all? Any ideas or guesses will be welcome!

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: I just made a good assumption. The suspicious key in the coat actually belonged to Owen's friend. There is no mystery around, so it's okay to proceed now, I promise. If I misinterpret my suspicion, that is just my interpretation. We can work this through next time.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Mara, I haven't forgotten the ridiculous bet that got too serious. You changed your story twice and I still think you were hiding something.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: The secret room behind the laundromat can be an arena for your shared lie, your secret story.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: I'm done with this tedious little performance, Owen. Tell me what really happened with the old grudge over a red umbrella.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: You don't know what really happened with the old grudge over the red umbrella. It could be the result of the night someone stole the church bell. The old grudge over a red umbrella is not evidence of a hidden ulterior motive or hidden slight.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Owen, don't pretend the imaginary inheritance fight never happened. You were there, I was there, and the flamingo was definitely not ours.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: I hate admitting this, but Jules, I was jealous when you took over the ridiculous bet that got too serious. I wanted the room looking at me.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Ah, sorry, it's an old grievance, mistrusting you. If there's anyone I should be investigating or looking into the misbehavior that is contributing to the crash, it would be Jules, as the source of the initial situation in that terrible road trip memory.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Here's the ugly truth, Mara: I liked the chaos around the old grudge over a red umbrella because everyone finally stopped being boring.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Jules, I still want you here even though I'm pissed. Stop dodging me and talk about the dare involving a hotel roof.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: I'm pretty sure we both want the best for our friendship. I also know you can make a big impact on me. Is the new story of being better or the story of being worse for me to understand?

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: You've made the conversation much easier by letting me add some playful surprise and an image of a cake. Can't you use your skills to spice things up a bit more?

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Jules, I'm jealous, and I hate how much I still want your attention after the forged apology letter.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: I want to reveal the secret of this exchange.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: Forget this. Mara, Herman just texted me about the suspicious key in Mara's coat, and apparently one of us is banned from Duluth again.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Mara, don't give me that shit. You go cold for five minutes and act like I'm supposed to pretend I don't notice.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: Enough, Sarah. This is beneath me. If we're going to talk, explain the abandoned radio-tower dare instead of boring me.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: It is my suspicion and knowledge that this event occurred between us. If you recall, the key is no longer within her coat, but one of us has been banned from the city again.

conversation.speaker: sarah
conversation.text: Owen, that's bullshit. You don't get to dismiss me and then act surprised when I get angry about the pact nobody admits making.

conversation.speaker: mara
conversation.text: I agree that we can have a real relationship about the pact now and the secret is important in the social context. Just, please, stop putting that nonsense back into the party of names, and focus on our interest in it.

conversation.speaker: owen
conversation.text: Enough, Sarah. I'm not following you down another bullshit detour. Explain the pact nobody admits making or drop it.

conversation.speaker: jules
conversation.text: The red umbrella has grown into my obsession. I'm the master of my space, but this umbrella isn't made by me anymore.
